//: Explicit classification for every composite index spec in migration/firestore/rules/firestore.indexes.json. Entries are keyed by index IDENTITY (collectionGroup, queryScope and the ordered field list), never by array position, so reordering or inserting a spec cannot change what any classification means. A spec with no entry here is REVIEW_REQUIRED and fails the dry-run index gate closed. classification values: HARD_REQUIRED_FOR_CORRECTNESS, REQUIRED_FOR_ACCEPTABLE_PERFORMANCE, REQUIRED_FOR_ACCEPTABLE_FREE_TIER_USAGE, COST_OPTIMIZATION, OPTIONAL, NOT_REQUIRED, REVIEW_REQUIRED. Only the hardDryRunGate entries block DRY_RUN_GO.

evidenceStates.MEASURED: Classification supported by a recorded measurement against the production corpus.
evidenceStates.REASONED_FROM_CORPUS: Classification derived from the recorded corpus size and the query's declared bound, without a production query plan.
evidenceStates.UNVERIFIED: No production measurement and no sufficient recorded reasoning. Fails closed.

classifications.rationale: The trips list is the common travel screen and pages 25 results. Enterprise executes unindexed queries, so the absence is a cost problem rather than a correctness one, but an unindexed scan of the recorded 99-trip corpus costs 117 conservative read units against 51 for the indexed page, and the cost scales with the tenant collection.
Same screen and the same 25-result page with a status filter applied; the unindexed cost is identical to the unfiltered list because the scan is what dominates.

classifications.query: FirestoreTravelDashboardRepository.listDashboardTrips: tenant, deletion state, payment-date range of the year.
classifications.rationale: Unresolved and deliberately not decided from resemblance. The query is genuinely reachable (Dashboard.tsx -> listDashboardTrips) and runs the same tenant and deletion predicates as the two gated indexes, but it is a year range bounded at DASHBOARD_TRIPS_BOUND = 2000 rather than a 25-result page, so its cost profile is not the same and cannot be inferred from the others. A production query plan would settle it; Enterprise rejects the Explain API used by the analyser (INVALID_ARGUMENT: Explain options are not supported in RunQuery API for Enterprise edition), so no measurement exists. An operator must classify it from a supported measurement before the index gate can pass.
classifications.operatorAction: Measure this query against the production corpus with a supported Enterprise mechanism, then set classification, hardDryRunGate and evidenceState accordingly.

classifications.query: FirestoreTravelRepository.listDueInstallments: tenant, active status set, due date.
classifications.rationale: The recorded corpus holds 37 installment rows, so a full scan costs 44 conservative read units. The index reduces that but its absence does not block a dry-run that writes no customer data. Revisit as the collection grows.
